blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Face de-identification (FDeID) has emerged as a critical privacy-preserving technology, yet its evaluation remains fundamentally fragmented.
Existing protocols rely on inconsistent metrics, heterogeneous datasets, and partial annotation coverage, so methods targeting different utility dimensions, such as landmark versus expression preservation, are reported on different benchmarks under different metrics, rendering cross-method comparison infeasible.
We revisit FDeID evaluation from both the data and metric perspectives. On the data side, we introduce UtilFace , a curated, demographically balanced benchmark with high identity diversity, assembled from four large-scale face datasets through identity-aware cleaning, resolution enhancement, and stratified filtering.
On the metric side, we propose HiFD , a Hi erarchical F ace D e-identification metric that unifies identity suppression, multi-level utility preservation, and image quality under a single consistency-based paradigm: every component is computed from pretrained estimators’ outputs on the original face and its de-identified counterpart, directly quantifying how much identity is suppressed and how much downstream-perceivable utility survives. HiFD organizes facial signals into a three-level utility hierarchy spanning macro cues (L1), micro cues (L2), and imperceptible cues (L3), and aggregates the five resulting components into a single interpretable score via weighted harmonic mean, with configurable application-specific profiles.
Using this unified protocol, we conduct a comprehensive comparative study spanning adversarial, GAN-based, and diffusion-based methods, surfacing trade-offs and failure modes that remain invisible under existing protocols.
We release the benchmark and evaluation toolkit to foster systematic and reproducible research in privacy-preserving human face analysis.
blocks.zh:
面相去识别(FDeID)作为一种关键的隐私保护技术已经出现,但其评价仍然基本上支离破碎.
现有协议依赖不一致的度量衡、不同的数据集和部分的注解范围,因此,针对不同效用维度的方法,如地标式和表达式保存,都报告在不同度量下的不同基准,使跨方法比较不可行。
我们从数据和衡量的角度重新审视FDEID的评价。 在数据方面,我们引入了UTIFace(UTIFace),这是一个具有高度身份多样性的精密,人口平衡的基准,通过身份意识清理,分辨率增强和分层过滤,从四个大型面相数据集组装而来.
在衡量方面,我们提出一个HIFD(Hi erarchical F Ace D)电子识别度量,它统一了身份压制,多层次的效用保存,以及基于一致性的单一范式下的图像质量:每个构件都是由预先经过训练的估算器在原始面上的输出及其去识别的对应物来计算的,直接量化了身份压制了多少以及下游可感知的效用存活了多少。 HIFD将面部信号组织成一个跨越宏提示(L1),微提示(L2)和不可见提示(L3)的三级效用等级,并通过加权口号平均值将所产生的五个组件汇总为单一可解释分数,并带有可配置的应用程序特有配置.
我们利用这个统一的协议,进行一项全面的比较研究,涉及对抗性方法、基于GAN的方法和传播方法、表面权衡和失败模式,这些模式在现有协议中仍然是看不见的。
我们发布了基准和评价工具包,以促进在保护隐私的人类脸谱分析方面进行系统和可复制的研究。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
The ubiquity of visual sensing in modern society has intensified the tension between advancing computer vision capabilities and privacy protection Hukkelås et al. (2019) ; Hasan et al. (2023) ; Gu et al. (2024) ; Jia et al. (2025) ; Laishram et al. (2025) .
Among all visual cues, human faces constitute uniquely identifying biometric signals and are captured pervasively by surveillance cameras, autonomous vehicles, and smart devices, often without explicit user consent Schroff et al. (2015) ; Deng et al. (2020) .
This reality has motivated extensive research on face de-identification (FDeID), which aims to modify facial imagery such that identity recognition is prevented while other task-relevant visual information is preserved for downstream applications Maximov et al. (2020) ; Lopez et al. (2024) ; Hinojosa et al. (2022) ; Zhou et al. (2025) .
Despite over two decades of active research, a fundamental question remains insufficiently answered: how private is private?

在所有视觉提示中,人脸构成独特的识别生物特征信号,并被监视相机、自主车辆和智能装置所普遍捕捉,往往未经用户明确同意。 Schroff等人(2015年); Deng等人(2020年)。

blocks.en:
Answering this question is hard because FDeID is inherently multi-objective. A successful method must not only suppress identity but also preserve various categories of facial utility, e.g. , age Geng et al. (2007) , gender Meng and Sun (2014) , expression Pan et al. (2024) , and landmarks Yang et al. (2024) , with the relevant subset depending on the downstream application. The community has responded by developing methods that each target a different subset of these utilities, and by evaluating each method on whichever dataset happens to carry the corresponding annotations. The result is a fragmented evaluation landscape in which a method optimized for expression preservation Yang et al. (2024) cannot be directly compared with one designed for detection preservation Jiang et al. (2023) , since they target fundamentally different utility dimensions on entirely different benchmarks Liu et al. (2025a) ; Wen et al. (2023) .
This fragmentation is reinforced by the absence of a unified benchmark: no existing dataset jointly provides the annotation coverage, identity diversity, and image quality required for reliable multi-dimensional evaluation Huang et al. (2008) ; Liu et al. (2015) ; Moschoglou et al. (2017) ; Karras et al. (2019) , so prior works have relied on heterogeneous task-specific datasets that produce mutually incompatible results.
For instance, A 3 GAN Zhai et al. (2022) evaluates expression preservation on ExpW Zhang et al. (2018b) , whereas SASMask Gong et al. (2023) assesses age preservation on AgeDB Moschoglou et al. (2017) , and the two simply cannot be meaningfully compared. We reviewed over 100 FDeID-related papers and quantified this fragmentation: more than 60 datasets and 20 evaluation metrics are used across prior protocols.

blocks.en: Beyond the fragmentation of what is measured, we identify a deeper concern in how utility is measured. Existing protocols cast utility preservation as the classification or regression accuracy of attribute predictions against externally annotated labels: a method is said to preserve expression if a classifier still predicts the annotated expression label on the de-identified image Yang et al. (2021) ; Salar et al. (2025) . This formulation is problematic on two counts. Operationally , it requires per-attribute ground-truth annotations on the evaluation dataset, which is precisely why no single benchmark suffices for multi-attribute evaluation (Tab. 1 ) and why the field has fragmented across task-specific datasets in the first place. Conceptually , it misaligns evaluation with deployment: what matters in practice is whether downstream models can still extract task-relevant information from the de-identified face, not whether their predictions match a static set of human annotations. We argue instead that utility should be measured by the consistency s ⁡ ( f ⁡ ( 𝐱 ) , f ⁡ ( 𝐱 ^ ) ) s(f(\mathbf{x}),\,f(\hat{\mathbf{x}})) between an attribute estimator’s predictions on the original face 𝐱 \mathbf{x} and its de-identified counterpart 𝐱 ^ \hat{\mathbf{x}} . This consistency-based formulation directly quantifies whether the information a model extracts from a face survives de-identification, eliminates the per-image annotation requirement, and unifies evaluation across attributes and datasets.
blocks.zh: 除了衡量的零碎问题外,我们发现对如何衡量效用有更深的担忧。 现有协议将功用保存作为属性预测相对于外注标签的分类或回归精度: 一种方法据说是,如果分类者仍然在去识别图像上预测附加说明的表达标签Yang等 (2021) ; Salar等 (2025) . 这种提法有两个问题。 在业务上,它要求对评价数据集进行每个属性的地面真实情况说明,这正是为什么没有一个单一的基准足以进行多属性评价(表1),以及为什么外地首先因具体任务数据集而分散。 从概念上讲,它把评价与部署错配:实际上重要的是下游模型是否仍然能够从去识别的面孔中提取出与任务有关的信息,而不是它们的预测是否与一套静态的人类说明相匹配. 相反,我们主张,应该用一个属性估计者对原始面x的预测与它被取消身份的对应者xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx 这种基于一致性的配方直接量化模型从面部取出的信息是否能活下来去识别,消除了每个图像的注释要求,统一了各种属性和数据集的评价.

blocks.en: Orthogonal to how utility is measured, we further observe that facial signals exhibit a natural hierarchy of perceptual granularity that existing protocols overlook (Fig. 2 ). Macro-level cues such as demographics and facial geometry are spatially coarse, semantically salient, and readily perceivable by human observers Moschoglou et al. (2017) ; Mollahosseini et al. (2017) . Micro-level cues such as gaze direction and micro-expressions depend on precise localized geometry and temporal dynamics that are far more fragile under facial manipulation Krafka et al. (2016) ; Zhao et al. (2023) . Imperceptible cues such as rPPG-based physiological signals, encoded in sub-pixel skin color variations, are the most susceptible to any image modification Stricker et al. (2014) ; Joshi et al. (2024) . This stratification suggests that FDeID methods affect each level differently, which a single scalar utility score cannot expose, motivating a hierarchical metric that evaluates preservation at all three granularities and surfaces the trade-offs between them.
blocks.zh: 就衡量效用而言,我们进一步观察到,面相信号表现出一种自然的感知颗粒结构,而现有协议忽略了这种结构(图2)。 人口学和面相几何等宏观层面的指针在空间上粗糙,有分光度,并易于被人类观察者Moschoglou等人(2017年);Mollahosseini等人(2017年)所察觉. 视线方向和微表情等微平面提示依赖于精确的局部几何和时间动态,在面部操纵下Krafka等(2016年);赵等(2023年)更为脆弱. 基于rPPG的生理信号等隐形提示被编码为子像素外观颜色变异,最容易被任何图像修改Stricker等(2014);Joshi等 (2024). 这种分层法表明,FDEID方法对每个级别的影响不同,一个单一的分级功用分数不能暴露出来,这刺激了一个分级度量法,它评价所有三个颗粒的保有量,并显示它们之间的取舍。

blocks.en: Based on the above observations, we make the following contributions: • UtilFace : a curated, balanced FDeID benchmark. We construct a face benchmark assembled from multiple large-scale datasets through identity-aware cleaning, resolution enhancement, and stratified filtering, providing a demographically balanced evaluation substrate with high identity diversity and image quality. We further integrate established video benchmarks (DFME Zhao et al. (2023) , PURE Stricker et al. (2014) ) to enable standardized evaluation across all utility levels. • A three-level facial utility hierarchy. We propose the first structured formalization of facial utility for FDeID, organizing signals into macro-cues (L1), micro-cues (L2), and imperceptible-cues (L3), and providing a principled lens for understanding which downstream tasks remain viable after de-identification (see Fig. 2 ). • HiFD: a unified, consistency-based metric. We introduce HiFD ( Hi erarchical F ace D e-identification metric), which integrates identity suppression, multi-level utility preservation, and image quality into an interpretable score via weighted harmonic mean aggregation, with application-specific weighting profiles and graceful adaptation across image and video modalities (see Fig. 1 ). • A comprehensive comparative study of FDeID methods. We evaluate representative adversarial, GAN-based, and diffusion-based methods under UtilFace and HiFD , surfacing trade-offs and failure modes that remain invisible under fragmented protocols.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 FDeID Methods
blocks.zh: 2.1 国防司 方法

blocks.en:
FDeID has evolved substantially from early approaches to sophisticated learning-based techniques.
Early methods employed simple image processing operations including pixelation, blurring, and masking Boyle et al. (2000) ; Hudson and Smith (1996) ; Letournel et al. (2015) ; Wei et al. (2026a) . While computationally efficient, these approaches fundamentally trade utility for privacy, degrading visual quality and destroying most facial information.
The k k -Same family of algorithms Gross et al. (2005) ; Gross et al. (2006) ; Meng and Sun (2014) ; Newton et al. (2005) introduced a principled privacy formulation based on k k -anonymity Sweeney (2002) , synthesizing faces that match at least k k individuals in a database. However, these methods produce visible artifacts and offer limited control over the privacy-utility trade-off.
Recent advances in generative modeling have enabled more nuanced approaches: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) Goodfellow et al. (2014) -based methods disentangle identity from attributes Maximov et al. (2020) , inpaint faces conditioned on surrounding context Hukkelås and Lindseth (2023) , or manipulate latent representations Agarwal et al. (2021) , while diffusion models Ho et al. (2020) offer improved fidelity and controllability Sun et al. (2024) .
Despite this methodological diversity, existing methods share a common evaluation blind spot: utility preservation is assessed in a fragmented manner, with each work measuring different attributes on different datasets using different metrics. Our benchmark addresses this gap through systematic, multi-level utility evaluation under a unified protocol.

blocks.en: 2.2 Evaluation Metrics and Protocols
blocks.zh: 2.2 评价计量和规程

blocks.en:
Evaluation of FDeID spans three dimensions: identity suppression, utility preservation, and image quality, each of which has accumulated
a heterogeneous collection of metrics. Identity suppression is most commonly reported as the de-identification success
rate Sharif et al. (2016) ; Khorzooghi and Nilizadeh (2023) ; Wang et al. (2024) ; Liu et al. (2025b) ; Salar et al. (2025) , with continuous or ranked
variants including recognition accuracy drop Li and Lyu (2019) ; Zhai et al. (2022) , cosine similarity Wen et al. (2022) ; Zhang et al. (2024) , identity distance Cao et al. (2023) ; Wen et al. (2023) ,
Rank- N N - T T Yang et al. (2021) ; Wang et al. (2025) , and AUC Meden et al. (2023) ; Proença (2022) ; Pan et al. (2024) , which differ
in normalization and recognizer dependence. Utility preservation is typically tied to the attribute being evaluated,
using categorical accuracy for expression Maximov et al. (2020) and classification or regression error for age and gender Gong et al. (2023) ; these protocols need annotations from different datasets (see Tab. 1 ). Image quality draws from reference-based metrics such as PSNR and SSIM Wang et al. (2004) , learned perceptual metrics such as LPIPS Zhang et al. (2018a) , and distributional metrics such as FID Heusel et al. (2017) . This proliferation of heterogeneous metrics and protocols impedes systematic comparison and reproducibility, while no existing metric provides a unified assessment across all three dimensions Wei et al. (2026b) . HiFD addresses both by adopting a consistency-based formulation and aggregating all three dimensions into a single interpretable score.

blocks.en: 2.3 Facial Signal Analysis
blocks.zh: 2.3 表面信号分析

blocks.en:
Facial images encode abundant information spanning identity features and non-identity utility cues across multiple granularities.
At the coarsest level, well-established tasks such as age estimation Geng et al. (2007) , gender classification Makinen and Raisamo (2008) , ethnicity recognition Karkkainen and Joo (2021) , expression recognition Li and Deng (2020) , and facial landmark detection Li et al. (2022) represent mature fields with established benchmarks and high-performing models; these macro-level signals are spatially coarse, semantically salient, and readily perceivable by human observers.
At a finer level, micro-expressions Zhao et al. (2023) and gaze direction Cheng et al. (2024) capture subtle behavioral and attentional states that are critical for affective computing, deception detection, and human-computer interaction; these signals depend on precise localized geometry and temporal dynamics that are far more fragile under facial manipulation. At the finest level, deep learning approaches for rPPG, including DeepPhys Chen and McDuff (2018) , PhysNet Yu et al. (2019) , and EfficientPhys Liu et al. (2023) , now recover heart rate and physiological waveforms from sub-pixel skin color variations in face videos, with transformative potential for telehealth and remote patient monitoring.

blocks.en: This natural stratification, from coarse attributes perceivable at a glance, through subtle behavioral dynamics, to physiological signals invisible to the naked eye, suggests an inherent hierarchy of facial signal that FDeID methods affect at different rates. Yet this hierarchical structure remains unexplored in FDeID evaluation. We formalize this observation and introduce a three-level utility framework that enables principled assessment of what facial information FDeID methods preserve or destroy.

blocks.en: 3.2 HiFD Metric
blocks.zh: 3.2 HIFD计量

blocks.en:
Evaluating FDeID requires jointly quantifying two competing objectives: how effectively identity is suppressed and how faithfully
non-identity information is retained .
Existing protocols report these objectives in isolation, treat utility as a monolithic concept, and often rely on ground-truth
labels.
We address these limitations with HiFD , a unified scalar metric that integrates identity suppression, hierarchical utility
preservation, and image quality into a single interpretable score. HiFD adopts a consistency-based formulation throughout: every component is computed as the consistency between a pretrained estimator’s outputs on the original input and its de-identified counterpart, directly quantifying the amount of downstream-perceivable information that survives de-identification.
We first define a generic consistency function, instantiate it on the three-level hierarchy, then specify privacy and quality, and combine all five into the composite HiFD score.

FDeID methods. We evaluate 12 representative methods spanning the three dominant FDeID paradigms based on their underlying generation mechanism.

blocks.zh: 4.2 主要成果

blocks.en: Tab. 3 reports HiFD and all sub-scores across the 12 evaluated methods. Five findings emerge that are invisible under existing fragmented protocols.

blocks.en:
Finding 1: The privacy-utility frontier is not monotonic across paradigms. No FDeID family dominates on both axes and each trades privacy for utility on its own terms.
Adversarial methods retain the highest macro-cue scores ( U 1 > 0.92 U_{1}>0.92 for PGD and MI-FGSM), as expected from their minimally visible pixel perturbations, but only the two with explicit transferability objectives reach P ¯ ≈ 0.50 \bar{P}\approx 0.50 (TI-DIM, TIP-IM). MI-FGSM and PGD stall at P ¯ < 0.14 \bar{P}<0.14 , suggesting that recent robust recognizers largely survive naive gradient attacks; in operational terms they de-identify only 8 % 8\% of faces at any false-accept rate (Appendix C.2 ).
GAN methods cover the widest privacy range: CIAGAN reaches P ¯ = 0.45 \bar{P}=0.45 by replacing the face entirely, but at severe cost on U 1 U_{1} ( 0.47 0.47 ) and landmarks ( 0.08 0.08 ), while cosmetic methods such as Adv-Makeup preserve macro-cues almost perfectly yet offer virtually no identity suppression ( P ¯ = 0.01 \bar{P}=0.01 ).
Diffusion methods sit between these extremes. WeakenDiff achieves P ¯ = 0.22 \bar{P}=0.22 and U 1 = 0.83 U_{1}=0.83 . DiffAM, despite its explicit adversarial-makeup objective, scores only P ¯ = 0.16 \bar{P}=0.16 on our ArcFace/CosFace/AdaFace ensemble, since its makeup perturbations were trained against IRSE50/IR152/MobileFace/FaceNet and transfer imperfectly to modern recognizers. DiffAM nonetheless outperforms WeakenDiff on U 2 U_{2} , U 3 U_{3} , and Q Q ( 0.81 0.81 , 0.56 0.56 , 0.47 0.47 ) and trails only marginally on U 1 U_{1} ( 0.79 0.79 vs. 0.83 0.83 ), yielding a higher HiFD of 0.394 0.394 versus 0.332 0.332 .

Finding 2: Hierarchical signals degrade at different rates. Preservation drops from L1 to L3 for almost every method, with the steepest collapse in generative families.
AMT-GAN, CIAGAN, G 2 Face, and WeakenDiff all score U 3 < 0.33 U_{3}<0.33 , confirming that face synthesis decouples macro appearance from fine-grained skin-color dynamics.
Adversarial methods preserve U 3 U_{3} best (TIP-IM 0.62 0.62 , Chameleon 0.80 0.80 ), since bounded ℓ ∞ \ell_{\infty} or ℓ 2 \ell_{2} noise leaves low-frequency skin signals largely intact.
Only Adv-Makeup ( U 3 = 0.93 U_{3}\!=\!0.93 ) and DeID-rPPG ( U 3 = 0.91 U_{3}\!=\!0.91 ) combine high U 3 U_{3} with high U 1 U_{1} , but both trade this preservation for a complete loss of identity suppression.

blocks.en:
Finding 3: Hierarchical preservation is asymmetrically coupled. Does retaining the strictest level U 3 U_{3} imply retention of U 2 U_{2} and U 1 U_{1} , and conversely? Fig. 5 answers across the 12 methods.
The parallel-coordinates panel (left) shows the polylines fanning out from U 1 U_{1} to U 3 U_{3} : nine of the twelve methods exceed 0.80 0.80 on U 1 U_{1} and nine on U 2 U_{2} , yet only Adv-Makeup and DeID-rPPG sit above U 3 = 0.90 U_{3}\!=\!0.90 , while AMT-GAN, CIAGAN, WeakenDiff, and G 2 Face fall below U 3 = 0.35 U_{3}\!=\!0.35 .
The conditional preservation matrix (right) quantifies the implication structure at threshold τ = 0.80 \tau\!=\!0.80 : every method that preserves U 3 U_{3} also preserves U 1 U_{1} and U 2 U_{2} ( Pr ⁡ ( U 1 ≥ τ | U 3 ≥ τ ) = Pr ⁡ ( U 2 ≥ τ | U 3 ≥ τ ) = 1.00 \Pr(U_{1}\!\geq\!\tau\,|\,U_{3}\!\geq\!\tau)=\Pr(U_{2}\!\geq\!\tau\,|\,U_{3}\!\geq\!\tau)=1.00 ), yet only 22 % 22\% (two of nine) of the methods that preserve U 1 U_{1} also preserve U 3 U_{3} ; the asymmetry holds for every τ ∈ [ 0.70 , 0.90 ] \tau\in[0.70,0.90] .
Practically, the asymmetry refutes the common shortcut of certifying L3 preservation by inspecting macro cues alone. This is precisely what the harmonic-mean aggregation enforces via the vetoing property: a near-zero U 3 U_{3} component cannot be masked by strong U 1 U_{1} scores, so methods are ranked by their weakest dimension rather than their average. TIP-IM achieves the highest HiFD of 0.607 0.607 for this reason: it is the only method that reaches at least 0.44 0.44 on every dimension simultaneously, while specialized methods such as DeID-rPPG ( U 3 = 0.91 U_{3}\!=\!0.91 ) and G 2 Face ( U 1 = 0.81 U_{1}\!=\!0.81 ) excel on a single axis but do not dominate the composite.

Finding 4: Application-specific profiles reshape the ranking. Tab. 5 reports HiFD under the three profiles defined in § 3.2 .
Under Privacy-First ( w P = 0.5 w_{P}\!=\!0.5 ), CIAGAN rises within the GAN family thanks to its strong identity suppression, yet TIP-IM still leads overall because its balanced profile avoids any near-zero component.
Under Clinical ( w 3 = 0.4 w_{3}\!=\!0.4 ), adversarial methods (TIP-IM, Chameleon) dominate as they retain physiological rPPG signals, while most GAN-based methods collapse since their face synthesis destroys sub-pixel dynamics regardless of visual fidelity.
Adv-Makeup and DeID-rPPG remain at the bottom across all profiles: despite excellent utility preservation, their near-zero identity suppression ( P ¯ < 0.02 \bar{P}<0.02 ) is mathematically penalized by the harmonic-mean aggregation.
The optimal FDeID choice therefore depends on which utility levels the downstream application prioritizes, but no profile rescues a method that fails on identity suppression.

Finding 5: FDeID methods are largely demographic-agnostic, with adversarial methods showing the largest disparities. Fig. 6 decomposes each method’s HiFD score across two genders and seven ethnicities.
Across all 12 methods, no single method shows a per-gender gap larger than 0.035 0.035 or a seven-way ethnicity range larger than 0.064 0.064 , both an order of magnitude below the inter-method spread in Tab. 5 .
The four methods with the widest per-method ethnicity range, PGD ( 0.064 0.064 ), Chameleon ( 0.050 0.050 ), MI-FGSM ( 0.049 0.049 ), and DiffAM ( 0.039 0.039 ), are all gradient-based or makeup-style perturbations that depend on local skin-tone gradients, which plausibly explains why they treat East Asian samples slightly differently from the rest.
The top-ranked TIP-IM (gender gap 0.006 0.006 , ethnicity range 0.014 0.014 ) and the bottom-ranked Adv-Makeup and DeID-rPPG
(disparities ≤ 0.021 \leq\!0.021 ) confirm that neither leadership nor failure is concentrated on any subgroup.
The results demonstrate that current FDeID methods, despite spanning three different generation paradigms, do not exhibit the demographic-specific failure modes that have been documented for face recognition itself. blocks.en: Every HiFD component is a consistency score , computed from a pretrained estimator’s outputs on 𝐱 \mathbf{x} and 𝐱 ^ \hat{\mathbf{x}} without any label. Its validity therefore rests on two questions: does the consistency score track true utility preservation, and does the privacy score correspond to an operational notion of privacy? Fig. 7 places the consistency score next to a ground-truth score for every method, using ground truth that is available outside UtilFace . For macro-expression (Fig. 7 a) we de-identified the labeled RAF-DB test set ( 3,068 3{,}068 images) with all twelve methods and compared the consistency score with the fraction of ground-truth accuracy the same estimator retains on the de-identified images: the two bars differ by at most 0.06 0.06 for every method, both place CIAGAN far below the rest, and both agree on the three best-preserving methods. Per image, the consistency score predicts whether the true label survives with AUC 0.98 0.98 over 28,614 28{,}614 pairs, and only 1.1 % 1.1\% of pairs with a consistency score above 0.8 0.8 hide a flipped label. For rPPG (Fig. 7 b), MMPD’s contact sensor gives the true heart rate, so the ground-truth bar is the fraction of heart-rate accuracy retained after de-identification. The two scores live on different scales, because heart-rate error saturates, but they order the methods the same way: the same three best (Adv-Makeup, DeID-rPPG, Chameleon, whose de-identification raises the true error by under 1 1 bpm) and the same three worst (AMT-GAN, CIAGAN, WeakenDiff, by 4.5 4.5 to 7.4 7.4 bpm), with eleven of twelve methods within one rank of each other. A consistency score can still mislead for near-tie posteriors, which flip the hard label under an arbitrarily small total-variation change, or for an estimator that is degenerate on the de-identified domain. The first is why we measured hidden flips, and the second is bounded by estimator substitution (Appendix C.4 ).

blocks.en: 4.4 How Private is Private?
blocks.zh: 4.4 私人是怎样的?

blocks.en: Our comparative study delivers a sobering answer: under the unified HiFD protocol, no current FDeID method is simultaneously private and utility-preserving across all three hierarchical levels. The best-performing method in our study, TIP-IM, attains a HiFD of only 0.607 0.607 , meaning that even the strongest baseline leaves a measurable gap on at least one of the five axes ( P ¯ , Q , U 1 , U 2 , U 3 \bar{P},Q,U_{1},U_{2},U_{3} ); every other method we evaluate scores below 0.52 0.52 . The privacy axis itself is the most fragile: nine of the twelve methods achieve P ¯ < 0.30 \bar{P}<0.30 against our three-recognizer ensemble, and only three de-identify more than 80 % 80\% of faces at a false-accept rate of 10 − 2 10^{-2} (Tab. 8 ), indicating that perceived “privacy” in much of the prior literature reflects evaluation against a single, often outdated recognizer rather than genuine identity suppression against modern systems. When privacy is achieved, it is typically purchased at a steep and uneven cost across the hierarchy, with macro cues (L1) most often retained, micro cues (L2) partially degraded, and physiological signals (L3) silently destroyed by virtually all generative approaches regardless of their visual fidelity. Consequently, we argue that future FDeID research should report HiFD alongside its constituent components rather than any single privacy or utility number in isolation.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented UtilFace and HiFD , a paired benchmark and hierarchical metric for face de-identification. UtilFace is a curated, demographically balanced corpus assembled from four large-scale sources. HiFD unifies identity suppression, three-level utility preservation, and image quality into a single consistency-based score, computed without per-image attribute annotations. A comparative study over 12 12 representative methods spanning adversarial, GAN-based, and diffusion-based families surfaces trade-offs invisible to existing protocols: hierarchical signals degrade asymmetrically, with macro cues mostly retained, micro cues partially degraded, and physiological rPPG silently destroyed by virtually all generative approaches; most adversarial methods, once evaluated against an ensemble of modern recognizers, exhibit limited identity suppression; and no current method is simultaneously private and utility-preserving across all three levels.

WebFace42M (research-only, non-commercial),
Glint360K (research-only),
MS1MV2 (research-only, derived from MS-Celeb-1M),
MegaFace (research-only, subject to the MegaFace Terms of Use).
Each of these licenses permits research use and derivative processing of the data, and none forbids the construction or distribution of derived identifiers such as identity keys and file lists.
We release UtilFace as a set of identity-indexed processing and sampling scripts together with the list of selected identity keys and image
filenames from each source, rather than as a redistributed image archive, so that downstream users obtain the underlying images
directly from the original providers under the original licenses and the release exposes nothing beyond the public sources. The release scripts, evaluation toolkit, and computed HiFD scores for all baseline methods are made available for research use.

blocks.en: The identity keys are opaque per-source indices and are useful only to someone who already holds the licensed source data. The release is gated behind the same research-only terms as the sources, the accompanying documentation states the intended use (evaluation of de-identification, not training of recognizers, not re-identification of individuals).

blocks.en: The intended positive impact is a common, annotation-free yardstick that lets privacy-preserving face analysis be compared and improved reproducibly, and that exposes silent failures ( e.g. , destroyed physiological signals) before deployment in telehealth or surveillance contexts. Two negative uses are foreseeable. First, a benchmark that scores identity suppression against modern recognizers can be used to tune methods whose purpose is to evade lawful face recognition; we consider this risk modest because the recognizers we ensemble are public and the adversarial methods we evaluate already exist, and because the same measurements are what defenders need. Second, any face benchmark concentrates biometric data; the release design above (no pixels, no embeddings, gated research-only terms, removal on request) is our mitigation. HiFD is a machine-recognizer score and should not be read as a guarantee of anonymity against human observers or future recognizers.
blocks.zh: 意图产生的积极影响是一个通用的、无注释的尺度,可以比较和再生地改进保护隐私的面部分析,并暴露在部署在远程保健或监视情况下之前的无声故障(例如被摧毁的生理信号)。 两种负面用途是可以预见的。 首先,一个对现代识别器进行身份压制的衡量基准,可以用来调整旨在逃避合法面相识别的方法;我们认为这一风险不大,因为我们的识别器是公开的,我们评价的对抗方法已经存在,因为同样的测量是捍卫者需要的。 其次,任何面谱基准都集中生物鉴别数据;上面的放出设计(没有像素,没有嵌入,只门式研究术语,应要求去除)是我们的缓解. HIFD是机器识别分数,不应被解读为对人类观察者或未来识别者匿名的保证.

blocks.en: MMPD and PURE ship contact-sensor pulse waveforms, so the true heart rate of every clip is known. For each method we compute the mean absolute HR error of the rPPG ensemble on the de-identified clips minus that on the originals ( Δ \Delta MAE, in bpm); a method that preserves the pulse leaves Δ \Delta MAE near zero. Ranking methods by − Δ -\Delta MAE agrees with the consistency-based U 3 U_{3} at Spearman 0.944 0.944 on MMPD ( 0.993 0.993 on PURE) with the same top three (Adv-Makeup, DeID-rPPG, Chameleon) and bottom three (AMT-GAN, CIAGAN, WeakenDiff) on both datasets (per-method values in Tab. 13 ). Among clips whose consistency score exceeds 0.8 0.8 , none has a de-identification-induced HR error above 10 10 bpm on either dataset ( 21,951 21{,}951 chunks on MMPD, 9,839 9{,}839 on PURE), so a high U 3 U_{3} never hides a destroyed pulse. In absolute terms the estimators, used without retraining, are weak on MMPD ( 34.3 34.3 bpm MAE on the originals against 21.9 21.9 bpm on PURE); the consistency score measures the change induced by de-identification, which is what the contact sensor validates, not absolute accuracy.

blocks.zh: C.6 质量轴心:无参考的替代品

blocks.en: Half of Q Q is LPIPS similarity to the original. Since successful identity replacement necessarily changes appearance, LPIPS could in principle conflate “changed the face” with “degraded the face”. We tested this with two measures that never see the original, BRISQUE Mittal et al. (2011) and TOPIQ face-IQA Chen et al. (2024) , on a paired 12,000 12{,}000 -image subset per method, and rebuilt a reference-free quality term Q nr Q_{\text{nr}} as the mean of the two normalized scores. Tab. 12 reports the results. Three observations. (i) LPIPS is not the mechanism penalizing replacement methods: dropping it moves the replacement family down on average (mean rank shift − 0.5 -0.5 ) and the perturbation family up ( + 0.5 +0.5 ), and CIAGAN falls from rank 6 6 to 9 9 rather than rising, because its quality deficit is visible without any reference (BRISQUE 80.9 80.9 and TOPIQ 0.250 0.250 against 38.4 38.4 and 0.752 0.752 for the originals, and the highest face-detection failure rate of any method, 0.7 % 0.7\% ). Genuinely clean appearance-changing methods score near the originals (Adv-Makeup 39.0 39.0 , AMT-GAN 39.4 39.4 ). (ii) The published and reference-free Q Q rank methods almost independently (Spearman 0.126 0.126 ): the two capture different things, fidelity to the source versus freedom from artifacts, which is why we report the sub-scores separately. (iii) The composite is insensitive to the choice: substituting Q nr Q_{\text{nr}} leaves Spearman 0.951 0.951 with the same top three, and removing Q Q altogether leaves 0.979 0.979 . The human study (Appendix E ) adds that LPIPS has no detectable rank association with human naturalness, so Q Q should be described as an artifact and fidelity term rather than a naturalness term.

blocks.en: D.3 L3 Replication on the MMPD Dataset

blocks.en: PURE has ten subjects, so we replicate the L3 evaluation on a larger dataset. We de-identified the full MMPD dataset Tang et al. (2023) ( 33 33 subjects, 655 655 trials, 392,832 392{,}832 frames after intersecting the keys common to all methods; frame-identical across conditions) with all twelve methods and re-ran the three rPPG estimators with no retraining. We deliberately did not use UBFC-rPPG, on which PhysNet, EfficientPhys, and FactorizePhys are trained, to avoid a train/test leak. MMPD is stratified by four illumination conditions (LED-low, LED-high, incandescent, natural) and five motion conditions (stationary, stationary after exercise, rotation, talking, walking), which lets us check that the family-level separation is not an artifact of one recording condition.
blocks.zh: PURE有十个主题, 所以我们复制 L3 评价 在更大的数据集。 我们解析了完整的MPD数据集Tang等人(2023年)(33个33个课题,655 655个试验,392 832 392{,}832个帧,在将所有方法共同的键相接后;跨条件的帧相同)与所有12个方法相接并重排了3个rPPG估计器,没有再培训. 我们故意没有使用UBFC-rPPG,PhysNet、高效Phys和FindexizePhys在其中接受了培训,以避免火车/测试泄漏。 MMPD通过四个发光条件(LED-low,LED-high,白炽,自然)和五个运动条件(固定,运动后固定,旋转,交谈,走走)进行分级,这让我们检查一下,家庭层面的分离不是一个记录条件的文物.

blocks.en: Appendix E Human Perceptual Study

blocks.en: HiFD is estimator-based. The study reported here asks whether its judgments agree with human perception on the three axes where a mismatch would matter most: (H1) does human naturalness track the reference-free quality terms rather than LPIPS; (H2) does human-judged attribute preservation track U 1 U_{1} , with the concrete counter-hypothesis that CIAGAN preserves demographics to a human despite its low U 1 U_{1} ; (H3) does the privacy score track human identity matching. It is not a validation of HiFD against human perception in general, and we report its limits with its results.

The defensible claim is the null: LPIPS similarity to the original has no detectable rank association with human naturalness. The reference-free alternatives do better (the paired gap BRISQUE minus LPIPS is + 0.49 +0.49 [ + 0.32 , + 0.62 ] [+0.32,+0.62] under the rater bootstrap), but with twelve methods even BRISQUE does not reach significance against method sampling, so we do not claim a validated naturalness proxy. HiFD (Balanced) itself correlates at − 0.62 -0.62 with human naturalness; this is the intended trade-off rather than a disagreement, since naturalness runs at − 0.66 -0.66 against P ¯ \bar{P} and + 0.91 +0.91 against U 1 U_{1} , and within the human data the same-person rate correlates at + 0.89 +0.89 with naturalness: the methods humans cannot see through are the ones they rate unnatural. HiFD does not, and should not, track naturalness.

HIFD(Balanced)本身在− 0.62-0.62与人类的自然性相关;这是预期的取舍而不是分歧,因为自然性在− 0.66-0.66与P'\bar{P}和+ 0.91+0.91与U1 U_{1}之间运行,在人类数据中,同人率在+ 0.89+ 0.89与自然性相关:人类无法看透的方法是他们认为不自然的方法。 家庭健康部没有,也不应该追踪自然。

blocks.en: Pooled over all twelve methods, the human same-person rate correlates with P ¯ \bar{P} at − 0.549 -0.549 ( p = 0.07 p=0.07 ) and with fixed-FAR success at only − 0.247 -0.247 . This pools two threat models. Within the five adversarial methods the Spearman correlation with fixed-FAR success is − 1.000 -1.000 , and within the seven generative methods (GAN-based and diffusion-based) it is − 1.000 -1.000 : humans reproduce the operational de-identification ranking exactly inside each paradigm. The pooled figure is low because adversarial methods are engineered to defeat a recognizer while remaining near-invisible to a person (PGD same-person rate 1.000 1.000 at P ¯ = 0.113 \bar{P}=0.113 ), whereas replacement methods change the face outright (CIAGAN 0.114 0.114 ). The correct statement is that P ¯ \bar{P} is a machine-recognizer privacy score, it ranks operational risk correctly within a paradigm, and humans are not the adversary it models.
blocks.zh: 在所有十二种方法中,人类同人率与P'\bar{P}在0.549-0.549(p=0.07p=0.07)时相关,固定的FAR成功率仅为0.247-0.247。 这个集合了两个威胁模型。 在五种对抗方法中,Spearman与固定-FAR的成功关系是-1 000-1 000,在7种基因方法(基于GAN和传播)中,它是-1 000-1 000:人类在每个范式中完全复制了实用的去识别排名。 集合数字较低,因为设计对抗方法是为了击败一个识别器,同时保持对一个人的接近隐形(PGD同人比率为1.000 1.000 at P' = 0.113\bar{P}=0.113 ),而替换方法则直接改变面相(CIAGAN 0.114 0.114 ). 正确的说法是,P'\bar{P}是一个机器识别隐私分数,它正确地将操作风险排在一个范式之内,人类不是它所模拟的对手.

blocks.en: No method hides identity from a human (same-person rate < 0.5 <0.5 ) while preserving attributes to a human ( > 0.7 >0.7 ). Only CIAGAN clears the identity bar, and it destroys the attributes doing so; every method that keeps attributes above 0.7 0.7 is still recognized as the same person by at least 61 % 61\% of raters. Sweeping the identity threshold over { 0.3 , 0.4 , 0.5 , 0.6 } \{0.3,0.4,0.5,0.6\} and the attribute threshold over { 0.5 , 0.6 , 0.7 , 0.8 } \{0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8\} leaves the set empty in all sixteen combinations; only at an identity threshold of 0.7 0.7 , meaning 70 % 70\% of raters still say “same person”, does any method qualify, which is not de-identification.

blocks.en: Krippendorff’s α \alpha is 0.42 0.42 on naturalness and 0.64 0.64 on artifacts; Fleiss’ κ \kappa on the attribute majority is 0.45 0.45 . The naturalness value is below the conventional 0.667 0.667 and must be read as such; two contributors are uneven block assignment (raters were not assigned round-robin, so 78 78 of 312 312 (identity, condition) cells are singly rated and one block drew no rater) and the compressed effective range (originals at 3.32 3.32 rather than at ceiling), which deflates α \alpha mechanically. Method-level correlations rest on twelve points, and the permutation p p -values are the conservative reading. Raters are a convenience sample rather than a demographically balanced panel. Every conclusion above survives all four exclusion rules (pre-specified, n = 22 n=22 ; none, n = 24 n=24 ; dropping the mis-specified check, n = 18 n=18 ; any single failure excludes, n = 9 n=9 ). For these reasons the study supports three specific claims (LPIPS is not what humans respond to; U 1 U_{1} is not too generous to attribute-destroying methods; P ¯ \bar{P} is a recognizer-side score) and one replication of the central finding, not a general validation of HiFD against human perception.
blocks.zh: Krippendorff的α-α为自然性0.42 0.42,而文物0.64 0.64;Fleiss的 o-kappa为属性多数0.45 0.45。 自然值低于常规的0.667 0.667,必须这样解读;两个贡献者是不平衡的块分配(鼠标没有被分配到圆形-robin,因此312 312个细胞中的78个(身份,条件)被单独地评分,一个块不抽出分数)和压缩有效范围(原始的分数为3.32 3.32,而不是上限),这机械地分出α\α. 方法层次的关联性以十二分为主,通通p-值为保守读取. 鼠标是一个方便样本,而不是一个人口平衡的面板。 以上每一项结论均保留了全部四条排除规则(预先规定,n=22n=22;无;n=24n=24;放弃错误规定检查,n=18n=18;任何单一失败排除,n=9n=9). 由于这些原因,研究支持了三个具体的说法(LPIPS不是人类的反应;U 1 U_{1}对属性-破坏方法并不太慷慨;P'\bar{P}是一个识别-侧分)和对中心发现的一个复制,而不是对HIFD与人类认知作一般验证.
